1. Objective The primary objective of this project is to develop a computational model using Python 
to estimate ethanol production from biomass through a stepwise chemical conversion process. The 
model translates a real chemical pathway into mathematical equations and implements them in 
executable code. The program accepts user-defined process parameters, performs the required 
calculations, displays the results in a structured summary, and generates visualisation graphs to 
support comparative analysis. The specific objectives are: • To model the stepwise conversion of 
biomass to ethanol (Biomass → Cellulose → Glucose → Ethanol). • To implement stoichiometric 
conversion factors and process efficiencies in the mathematical model. • To generate and display at 
least one graph showing ethanol yield as a function of varying process efficiency. • To enable 
sensitivity analysis by varying hydrolysis and fermentation efficiencies across multiple data points. 2.

Process Overview Bioethanol production from lignocellulosic biomass involves a series of 
biochemical and chemical conversion stages. The model implemented in this project follows the 
pathway shown below: Biomass → (Cellulose Extraction) → Cellulose Cellulose → (Hydrolysis) → 
Glucose Glucose → (Fermentation) → Ethanol Each stage is governed by a stoichiometric conversion 
factor and a user-defined process efficiency parameter. The efficiency values represent real-world 
limitations such as incomplete enzymatic hydrolysis or microbial fermentation losses.
